newsitem.title: USA: North Calif. voters consider school bonds, taxes.
newsitem.headline: North Calif. voters consider school bonds, taxes.

text.p: Voters in northern California will go to the polls Tuesday to decide several school bond and tax measures, according to a published report.
The San Francisco Chronicle reported that Pleasanton voters will decide the fate of Measure B, a $70 million bond measure to fund school improvements.
In San Leandro, voters will consider Measure A, a $54 million school bond.
Measure C in Piedmont would allow the Piedmont Unified School District to levy a tax that would generate nearly $2 million per year over the next four years.
Piedmont's Measure D is also a four-year tax, but it would provide money to maintain school buildings. It would raise about $500,000 annually, the Chronicle reported.

The Burlingame Elementary District would cut class sizes, modernize its schools and reopen an 89-year-old facility if voters on Tuesday approve a pair of parcel taxes and a $6 million bond measure, the newspaper reported.
In Marin and Sonoma counties, about a dozen property tax measures to maintain fire protection services, improve schools and fix water delivery systems will go before the voters.

Many of Tuesday's measures are on the ballot because of Proposition 218, a statewide initiative approved last November. The proposition requires voter approval of an array of taxes, assessments and fees levied by local governments.
